narrative.h2: The 3D look that used to need a render farm

sections.heading: What 3D actually means in 2026
sections.body: Calling a video '3D' covers a wide spread - Pixar's character lighting, Unreal Engine 5 environments, Octane-rendered product shots, Beeple's daily surrealism. They share a tell: physically-based materials with real subsurface scattering, depth of field that resolves correctly through hair and glass, and shadows that respect the light source. When those three things break, the eye notices before the brain does. Everything else is style on top of that foundation.

sections.heading: Where the look comes from
sections.body: The reference shelf is well-established: Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse for stylized shading, Love, Death & Robots' Sonnie's Edge for character realism, Pixar's RenderMan for skin and cloth, Blender's Cycles renders that flood Reddit's r/blender weekly. Music-video specific: The Weeknd's Heartless and Travis Scott's Astroworld assets pulled from Unreal. Tunee's 3D model trains on this vocabulary, so prompts like 'Octane render, depth of field, soft area light from window left' land where a TD would aim them.

sections.heading: Prompting tip for Tunee
sections.body: Specify the render engine in the prompt even if it's metaphorical - 'Octane render', 'Unreal Engine 5 lumen', 'Pixar RenderMan'. Each pulls a different set of conventions for light falloff and material response. Then name your light setup explicitly: key, fill, rim. Skipping this is why generated 3D often looks flat or plasticky. Add 'shallow depth of field' only if your subject is one thing - wider scenes need it off.
